_readme: PROVISIONING settings for the PRD environment. Read by every `-Env prd` call in
This is NOT the pac import settings file. Two different kinds of settings file live
in this folder and they are consumed by different tools:
• <env>-settings.json  (this file) — read by the PowerShell scripts in
provisioning/ via Get-ProvisioningSettings. Describes Entra groups, Dataverse
group teams, role bindings, auditing, retention jobs and setting rows.
• pac-import-prd.json — passed to `pac solution import --settings-file`. Supplies
environment variable VALUES and connection reference bindings at solution
Identifiers only — never a secret, token or connection string (C-TECH-001). The
provisioning app id and certificate thumbprint stay in the environment variables
Every {{PLACEHOLDER}} must be replaced with the real per-environment value before
the pipeline runs: Get-Setting fails fast on any value that still contains {{...}}
(C-TECH-031 / C-TECH-047). Values that are POLICY rather than per-environment
(retention periods, audit retention days, the fixed scoring maps) are real values
here by design — they must be identical in every environment.
_unresolved_note: Keys knowingly left as {{...}} tokens, each owned and dated. Read by check 11 of
the FAIL and is REPORTED on every run; an entry that is missing, unowned or past its
expiry FAILS. Established 2026-08-21 after IMP-0145 — a placeholder that everyone knew
about and nobody owned survived a full day and cost a seeding pass.
THE SEVEN ENTRA IDS BELOW WERE ADDED 2026-08-21 (IMP-0175) AFTER TRYING TO RESOLVE THEM.
They were declared rather than filled in because this machine could not ground-truth them
on that date: `Get-MgContext` returns nothing (no Graph session), there is no `az` CLI, and
PROVISION_APP_ID / PROVISION_CERT_THUMBPRINT are unset, so no app-only Graph token can be
minted either. Every one of them IS resolvable in a single read-only Graph session by
whoever has one — the exact query is written into each entry's `why`. What was deliberately
NOT done is paste a commonly published GUID from memory: an incorrect permission id grants a
permission nobody reviewed, and IMP-0011's lesson is that a plausible-looking id is the most
expensive kind of wrong. Both target environments already exist (`pac admin list`,
2026-08-21: REV-GrantApplications-ACC and -PRD), so these are lookups, not blocked work,
which is why they carry a SHORT four-week expiry rather than a phase date.
GITHUB_ORG / GITHUB_REPO are NOT listed below because they were resolved for real from
`git remote -v` — see _comment_subject_resolved on the federated credential.

_unresolved.why: The Dataverse `user_impersonation` delegated-scope id on rev-grantautomation-deploy-prd. Resolve with one read-only Graph call: GET /servicePrincipals(appId='00000007-0000-0000-c000-000000000000')?$select=oauth2PermissionScopes — Dynamics CRM exposes exactly one scope, and its `id` is the value. Not written from memory on purpose: an incorrect permission GUID requests a permission nobody reviewed (IMP-0011).
_unresolved.expiry_rationale: Short because this is a lookup, not a decision or a build. It is also the one that must not be discovered late: ensure-app-registration.ps1 throws on the first read of this key, and the first PRD run is the worst place to find that out.

_unresolved.why: The SharePoint Online `Sites.Selected` APPLICATION-role id on REV-MS-Provisioning. Resolve with GET /servicePrincipals(appId='00000003-0000-0ff1-ce00-000000000000')?$select=appRoles and take the entry whose `value` is Sites.Selected. Note the trap this placeholder protects against: Microsoft Graph publishes a DIFFERENT Sites.Selected role id under appId 00000003-0000-0000-c000-000000000000, and pasting that one would consent the wrong resource entirely (ADR-018 chose SharePoint, not Graph).
_unresolved.expiry_rationale: Short — a lookup. Same run as the entry above; one Graph session clears every id in this block.

It is the identical GUID and is still a separate declaration, because the two registrations are consented separately and a copy-paste into only one of them is exactly how half a permission set ships.

Resolve with GET /servicePrincipals?$filter=displayName eq 'Microsoft Flow Service'&$select=appId,oauth2PermissionScopes. This file's own _comment_lookup already names the commonly published value and instructs the reader to CONFIRM it against the tenant rather than trust it; that instruction is what this declaration keeps enforceable instead of decorative.

Two values from one query, declared separately so a partial paste fails the gate rather than shipping.

Resolve with GET /groups?$filter=displayName eq 'REV-PP-GrantApplications-Admins-PRD'&$select=id, or let ensure-groups.ps1 create it and print the id (it reports EXISTS rather than CREATED if the manual precursor is already there). Never invented: a wrong group object id binds Dataverse security roles to the wrong set of people in PRODUCTION, which is a live access-control defect rather than a broken deploy.

KnockoutThreshold is a board decision, SDD OQ-001, not yet taken. seed-settings.ps1 must fail fast and write NOTHING rather than seed production with a guessed eligibility threshold — an auto-reject decided by a made-up number is a real decision about a real applicant.

entra._comment: Phase 1 groups only. rev-Finance-* and rev-Trustees-* are NOT created in this phase: no Phase 1 table is reachable by either persona. Group MEMBERSHIP is owned by the business/IAM process, never by the pipeline.
_comment_appRegistrations: App registrations still LIVE at tenant level - Entra has no per-environment scope - but
AS OF 2026-08-12 THIS BLOCK IS NO LONGER IDENTICAL to test-settings.json. The deploy
identity has been SPLIT ONE PER TARGET ENVIRONMENT (ADR-007): this file declares
rev-grantautomation-deploy-prd, test-settings.json declares -tstacc, and -dev is created
by hand alongside the DEV environment because Phase 1 has no dev-settings.json.
Consequence for the run order: the two runs of ensure-app-registration.ps1 are no longer
'create, then prove idempotency'. Each run creates a different deploy registration and
reports EXISTS for the shared ones, so BOTH runs' output must be read. Both remain
idempotent (C-TECH-042); what changed is that the second run is not a pure no-op.
What IS per environment is the Dataverse application user, created by
provisioning/dataverse/ against each environment.
PERMISSION IDS ARE {{PLACEHOLDER}} TOKENS ON PURPOSE, matching
dev-settings.example.json. The app-role GUIDs are stable across tenants but they are not
written here from memory: an incorrect GUID would grant a permission nobody reviewed.
Look each one up in the tenant (Graph: `GET /servicePrincipals(appId=...)?$select=appRoles`)
and paste it in. Every script fails fast while a token remains (C-TECH-047), so this
cannot be forgotten silently.
Least privilege is justified in TAD section 6.7 and ADR-018 (C-TECH-043):
Sites.Selected instead of Sites.FullControl.All, and Group.Create +
GroupMember.ReadWrite.All instead of Directory.ReadWrite.All.
GroupMember.ReadWrite.All is tenant-wide and is the narrowest permission that can manage
group membership - which is why ADR-018 justifies it explicitly rather than assuming it.

appRegistrations._comment: THE PRODUCTION DEPLOY IDENTITY, AND ONLY PRODUCTION. Renamed and split from the former single shared `rev-grantautomation-deploy` on 2026-08-12 (ADR-007). Solution import/export and Power Platform Pipelines promotion into PRD. Its authority in Dataverse comes from an APPLICATION USER IN PRD ONLY, holding a least-privilege deployment role - NOT System Administrator, and not a broad API permission (TAD section 6.7). No other environment's CI job can obtain a token for this identity, because the single federated credential below is bound to the `prd` GitHub Environment subject.
appRegistrations._comment_why_split: Scoping several federated credentials onto ONE app registration would gate token ISSUANCE but not AUTHORITY - every subject would still resolve to a single service principal that is an application user in every environment, so a token minted by the tst_acc CI job could import into PRD. This is the environment where that mattered most: PRD holds real special-category applicant data. Splitting the registration moves the boundary to 'the TST/ACC identity does not exist in PRD at all' (C-TECH-043).

requiredResourceAccess._comment: Dataverse / Dynamics CRM. Scope user_impersonation, per TAD section 6.7.

resourceAccess._comment: Permission: user_impersonation (delegated Scope). Look up the id on the Dataverse service principal.

federatedCredentials._comment: C-TECH-044 RESOLVED 2026-08-12 - this credential is now the one actually in use, and no client secret exists on this registration. .github/workflows/ci.yml authenticates with `pac auth create --githubFederated`, which needs only the application id and tenant id.
federatedCredentials._comment_subject: THE SUBJECT IS THE GITHUB ENVIRONMENT, NOT A BRANCH. GitHub's OIDC `sub` claim is `repo:ORG/REPO:environment:NAME` for any job that references an environment (https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/oidc), and Entra matches subjects as EXACT STRINGS with no wildcards. The previous value here was `ref:refs/heads/main`, which would never have matched a workflow that triggers on `feature/**`. EXACTLY ONE credential belongs on this registration: a second subject would let another GitHub Environment's job authenticate as the production deploy identity, which is precisely the hole splitting the registrations closed.
federatedCredentials.name: github-actions-env-prd
federatedCredentials._comment_subject_resolved: RESOLVED 2026-08-21 from ground truth, not from memory: `git remote -v` in this repository returns https://github.com/Argelis-XVL/Revitalise.git, so the org is Argelis-XVL and the repo is Revitalise; the environment segment is `prd`, the GitHub Environment name .github/workflows/ci.yml actually declares. Entra matches this subject as an exact string with no wildcards, so if the repository is ever renamed or transferred this value must be re-read from the remote and re-pasted — a stale subject fails token exchange with an authentication error that names nothing (IMP-0175).
federatedCredentials.subject: repo:Argelis-XVL/Revitalise:environment:prd

appRegistrations._comment: Signed with the certificate at PROVISION_CERT_THUMBPRINT (C-TECH-044). Original scope was Entra group creation, but ALL Phase 1 Entra groups (environment gates + persona/role groups) ended up created manually by the reviewer throughout this engagement — see prd-settings.json's own group entries below, each annotated 'already created manually'. As of 2026-08-14 the reviewer confirmed they cannot grant admin consent for Microsoft Graph application permissions on this tenant (role limitation, not a preference), so the Group.Create / GroupMember.ReadWrite.All permission block that used to sit here was REMOVED rather than left unconsentable and unused (least privilege, C-TECH-043 — don't request a permission nothing exercises). If a later phase needs scripted group creation after all, the permission block that was here is preserved in git history (see the commit that removed it) rather than re-derived from memory.
appRegistrations._comment_dataverse: The Dataverse permission below is what this registration is actually used for now: ensure-schema.ps1 (provisioning/dataverse/) authenticates with this SAME PROVISION_APP_ID/PROVISION_CERT_THUMBPRINT credential to call the Dataverse Web API metadata endpoints. Mirrors the Dataverse permission block already declared on the rev-grantautomation-deploy-* registrations below: 'Dynamics CRM' only ever exposes ONE permission, user_impersonation, shown as a Delegated Scope in the Entra portal even when it backs an app-only client-credentials grant — there is no separate Application-type Dataverse permission to request. ensure-schema.ps1 itself is DEV-only and is not expected to run against PRD (Power Platform Pipelines promotes the schema forward instead) — this permission is added here purely for consistency, since REV-MS-Provisioning is one shared tenant-level registration declared identically in both settings files. CONFIRMED WORKING 2026-08-14: live WhoAmI call against DEV succeeded once the application user was added there.

requiredResourceAccess._comment: SharePoint Online. Sites.Selected, chosen specifically to avoid Sites.FullControl.All (ADR-018). Scoped to /sites/grants when that site is created. Retained despite the Graph-consent limitation noted above because it is a DIFFERENT resource (SharePoint, not Graph) — consent for this one has not yet been attempted.
Dataverse / Dynamics CRM — ADDED 2026-08-14, consistency only (see _comment_dataverse above).

resourceAccess._comment: Permission: user_impersonation (delegated Scope) — the only Dataverse permission that exists.

appRegistrations._comment: ALEX'S WORDPRESS SITE AS AN OAUTH CLIENT-CREDENTIALS CALLER, and the identity the PRIMARY authentication control on the intake endpoint is built around (NFR-008, C-TECH-006). Created by provisioning/entra/ensure-intake-client.ps1, which also PRINTS the two identifiers the control needs: the application (client) id goes into the rev_IntakeAllowedClientId environment variable (the flow's second gate) and the SERVICE PRINCIPAL OBJECT ID goes into the trigger's 'Allowed users' field (the platform-level primary gate). They are different values and are not interchangeable. THIS BLOCK IS IDENTICAL TO test-settings.json ON PURPOSE: the registration is tenant-level and there is ONE WordPress site, so TST/ACC and PRD share the caller identity. What differs per environment is the trigger setting itself and the endpoint URL - see the `intake` block below.
appRegistrations._comment_adr011: ADR-011 IS STILL OPEN. This registration is the DEFAULT implementation, not the closed decision: the Entra OAuth route is now fully provisioned and testable, and the final intake channel choice is pending the conversation with Alex (the website developer). If that conversation lands on the shared-secret route or on the scheduled REST-pull route, DELETE this entry, the `intake` block below, provisioning/entra/ensure-intake-client.ps1 and provisioning/entra/verify-intake-endpoint-auth.ps1 together - leaving any of them behind creates an unused identity in the tenant and a smoke test that guards nothing. Dev Summary section 7, decision D-1.
appRegistrations._comment_credential: THE CALLER'S OWN CLIENT CREDENTIAL IS NOT PROVISIONED HERE AND IS NOT IN THIS REPOSITORY. Alex's site needs a certificate (preferred, C-TECH-044) or a client secret to obtain a token; it is issued interactively by the tenant administrator and handed over out of band. A pipeline that mints a credential is a pipeline that prints one (C-TECH-001). ensure-intake-client.ps1 reports whether one exists, by COUNT only.

requiredResourceAccess._comment: MICROSOFT FLOW SERVICE (Power Automate). Required so that Entra will issue this app a token whose aud claim is the Power Automate audience - without a declared permission on this resource, a client-credentials request for https://service.flow.microsoft.com//.default is refused and the endpoint cannot be called at all.
requiredResourceAccess._comment_lookup: PLACEHOLDER ON PURPOSE, per the block header above - not written from memory. Resolve both values in the tenant: `GET /servicePrincipals?$filter=displayName eq 'Microsoft Flow Service'&$select=appId,oauth2PermissionScopes`. The appId is commonly published as 7df0a125-d3be-4c96-aa54-591f83ff541c - CONFIRM that against the tenant rather than trusting it, then paste. The scope to take is the one named `User`.

resourceAccess._comment: Permission: User (delegated Scope) on Microsoft Flow Service. ⚠ ONE ITEM TO CONFIRM ON FIRST RUN: every published walkthrough of this pattern declares the DELEGATED `User` scope and then acquires an APP-ONLY token with `.default`, which is an unusual combination. If Entra refuses the client-credentials request, the fix is to grant the equivalent APPLICATION permission on the same resource and change `type` here to `Role`. Recorded rather than assumed - do not discover this in PRD.

Persona: process owner / administrator — PRD. Backs the REV Admins Dataverse group team. Already created manually by the reviewer on 2026-08-14 — ensure-groups.ps1's check-before-create will report EXISTS, not CREATED, for this one.

Persona: unattended automation service account — PRD. Backs the REV Service Accounts Dataverse group team. Already created manually by the reviewer on 2026-08-14 — ensure-groups.ps1's check-before-create will report EXISTS, not CREATED, for this one.

Persona: trustee — PRD. Backs the REV Trustees Dataverse group team. NEW 2026-08-21, WBS 6.1 — TAD §12 recorded this role group as deliberately NOT created in Phase 1 ('no Phase 1 table is reachable by this persona'); that changes now because rev_review arrives under WBS 6.4 and the trustee role (this feature) has a table to read. Unlike the two rows above, this group has NOT been created manually yet — ensure-groups.ps1 will attempt New-MgGroup and report CREATED, or FAILED if the provisioning identity still lacks Graph Group.ReadWrite.All consent (IMP-0105 — Connect-ProvisioningGraph succeeding here is not evidence this call will succeed). Do not create this in PRD ahead of a real, access-tested trustee app in TST/ACC (EX-003) — DEV/TST-only, test data only, until DPO sign-off and automation #5 both land.

_comment: THE PRIMARY AUTHENTICATION CONTROL ON THE SOLUTION'S ONE PUBLIC ENDPOINT
(NFR-008, C-TECH-006). Added 2026-08-12 to close test-agent defect D-001.
Read the same block in test-settings.json for the full reasoning; the values
below are identical except for the endpoint URL variable, because the control
is the same control and weakening it in PRD would be the wrong way round.
IT IS A TRIGGER SETTING, NOT A SOLUTION COMPONENT — it cannot ship in the
managed solution, so it is declared here, applied by a named owner as a
post_deploy step, and verified after every deployment by
⚠ PRD-SPECIFIC ORDER OF OPERATIONS. The flow imports switched OFF and is turned
on only after the connection references are bound. Configure the trigger
authentication parameter BEFORE turning the flow on: between switch-on and
configuration the endpoint is live and, by Power Automate's own default for a
newly authored trigger, may accept any tenant caller. The smoke test runs after
both steps and is what proves the window was closed.
ADR-011 remains OPEN: this is the default implementation, not the settled

triggerAuthentication._comment_mode: 'Anyone' is a defect. 'Any user in my tenant' would let ANY identity in the Revitalise tenant write applications into Dataverse, which is not least privilege for a single external caller. ⚠ Leaving the Allowed users field BLANK under this mode silently widens the scope back to the whole tenant, per Microsoft's own note — the smoke test cannot detect that, so it is called out here.
triggerAuthentication.allowedCallerSource: Service principal OBJECT id of intake.clientAppDisplayName — printed by provisioning/entra/ensure-intake-client.ps1. Not the application (client) id, and not the App-registrations Object ID: the Enterprise-applications one.
triggerAuthentication._comment_scope: Public-cloud values, and both are exact-match sensitive: the aud claim keeps its trailing slash, and the client-credentials scope therefore carries a DOUBLE slash before .default.
triggerAuthentication.configuredBy: Wanstor (tenant administration) applies it in the Power Automate designer for the PRD environment, inside the APPROVE PRD gate; Xander Lykopoulos (maker / Argelis Consultancy) supplies the service principal object id from the ensure-intake-client.ps1 output and confirms the smoke test passes before the endpoint is given to Alex. Recorded per C-TECH-041 so the control has a named owner, which is what D-001 found missing.

intake._comment_endpointUrl: THE TRIGGER URL IS A CREDENTIAL AND IS DELIBERATELY NOT A VALUE IN THIS FILE. It carries its own SAS signature in the `sig=` query parameter, which is why Microsoft documents regenerating it. Held as a CI secret under this name (C-TECH-001/047).

Declared here as the reviewed record of the binding for when this environment is actually promoted to — see contract/known-exceptions.json EX-003: the trustee portal stays in DEV with synthetic test data only until DPO sign-off is received AND automation #5 (narrative redaction) lands. columnSecurityProfiles._comment: The profile ships in the managed solution; only its membership is provisioned. These two teams are the only principals that may read or write the Tier 4 secured columns (TAD §6, NFR-001).

auditing._comment: 6 years = 2192 days (C-DOM-010, C-DOM-011, TAD §6.5). A longer period — and -1, retain forever — would keep applicant data in audit history after the record itself was deleted, so this number is reviewed with the DPO, not defaulted in code.

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Rejected Applications
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applications with status Rejected once rev_decisiondate is older than 12 months (C-DOM-003, ADR-004).

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Withdrawn or Incomplete Applications
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applications with status Withdrawn or Incomplete once the parent applicant's rev_lastcontactdate is older than 6 months (C-DOM-003, ADR-004).

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Orphaned Applicants
bulkDeleteJobs._comment: No retention period of its own: an applicant with no remaining application inherits the period of whichever job deleted the last child. Runs after the two application sweeps (TAD §3.4 gap 1).
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes applicant records that have no remaining child application — the derived orphan sweep.

bulkDeleteJobs.name: REV Retention - Error Log
bulkDeleteJobs.description: Deletes error log rows once rev_occurredon is older than 90 days. Error rows contain no personal data (C-DOM-004).

_comment_pending_setting_rows: KnockoutThreshold, BorderlineBandLower/Upper and IncomeCeiling deliberately carry
not agreed those figures yet (SDD OQ-001, OQ-002, OQ-003), so seed-settings.ps1
must fail fast and write NOTHING rather than seed production with unconfirmed
eligibility criteria — an auto-reject decided by a guessed threshold is a real
decision about a real applicant. The APPROVE PRD pre_deploy step requires the
figures to be recorded before this file is completed. Replacing a token is a
settings change, not a code change: no re-deployment is needed.
The other six rows are fixed by FR-011/FR-012/FR-013 or are reference data, so
they carry their real values and are identical to TST/ACC.

settingRows.description: Maps a wellbeing answer's option VALUE to circumstance points (FR-013). Position 1 scores 5, position 5 scores 1. Key "6" ('Not sure') = 0, CHANGED FROM 0.5 on 2026-08-20 and confirmed with Emily (process owner). This supersedes the D-014 derivation from the hand-scored export; the map now holds no fractional value, so the half-point rounding can never fire. Full record: provisioning/deploymentSettings/settings-rows.notes.md#LikertPointMap.

Inverts the life-satisfaction answer rev_feelingscaleanswer, a whole number 0 to 10, so that a lower reported satisfaction scores more points (FR-012). This is 10 minus the raw answer, expressed as a lookup map so the direction of the scale is configuration rather than arithmetic inside the flow. REPLACED IN REVISION 0.3: it was a five-entry map over a five-option picklist. The Automation Solution Design v0.5 specifies exactly this for Automation #2 Q1 — "inverted (0/10 feeling = 10 points)".
Circumstance score at or below which the application status becomes Auto-reject. Board decision, SDD OQ-001.
Lower bound (inclusive) of the Borderline review band. Board decision, SDD OQ-002.
Upper bound (inclusive) of the Borderline review band; a score above it becomes Auto-pass. Board decision, SDD OQ-002.
Annual household income ceiling in GBP. Board decision, SDD OQ-003.

Maps an age in whole years to a rev_agerange option value (1=Under 18 .. 8=75 and over). Fixed reference data. Option 9 (Not known) is the fallback when no date of birth was supplied and is therefore not in the map.

Maps the age-band labels the live form actually sends to rev_agerange (2=18-24 .. 8=75+, 9=Not known). The live form asks an age band directly, NOT a date of birth, so this map — not AgeBandMap — is the primary route to rev_agerange. Matched case-insensitively after trimming. Option 1 (Under 18) has no label (form gates on 18+). Full derivation kept in provisioning/deploymentSettings/settings-rows.notes.md#AgeRangeLabelMap (D-021).

An unmatched label leaves the column empty rather than guessing. Full derivation: settings-rows.notes.md#EmploymentStatusLabelMap.

Maps the care-hours band labels the live form sends to rev_carehoursperweek option values (FR-064, form-field-corrections pass). Matched case- and dash-insensitively after trimming - the live form and other sources render band 2's dash differently. An unmatched label leaves the column empty. Full derivation: settings-rows.notes.md#CareHoursBandLabelMap.

Maps the uppercased alphabetic prefix of a UK outward code to a rev_locationarea option value (1=North East .. 12=Northern Ireland). Longest prefix wins, so match SW before S. Fixed reference data. Option 13 (Not known) is the fallback for an unrecognised or absent postcode and is therefore not in the map.

Maximum attainable circumstance score, for rendering 'n out of N': 10 wellbeing answers x 5 (50) plus the inverted life-satisfaction answer up to 10 = 60 (FR-011). Confirmed 60, not 55 — life-satisfaction is the 0-10 scale its source describes; matches the raw export header and Automation Solution Design v0.5. Unblocks KnockoutThreshold and the Borderline band (SDD OQ-001/002). Full derivation kept in provisioning/deploymentSettings/settings-rows.notes.md#MaxCircumstanceScore (D-021).

Maps each rev_incomeband option to the top of that band, compared against IncomeCeiling (FR-015). NFR-019: if the form's income bands change, this row changes, not the scoring flow. Option 5 (40,000+) is unbounded with a sentinel above any realistic ceiling; option 6 (Prefer not to say) carries -1, mapped to income flag 3, not a guess. _comment_trusteeCodeAppAbsent: The trustee Code App (WBS 6.1) is intentionally absent from dataverse.apps[] even
though WBS 6.5 is active. It is added only after a real `pac code push` has assigned
an appId: running `share-apps.ps1 -Env prd` with a {{TRUSTEE_CODE_APP_ID}} placeholder
would cause a post_deploy step (which is live and wired for PRD) to throw at
Get-Setting time, failing a deploy that works today. Assumption A-TR-3 in
share-apps.ps1 forbids inventing a platform-assigned id (C-TECH-051). The two-step
closure sequence — first publish the app to assign an id, then add the entry — is in
block. That ordering guarantees the id is real before it is configured.

_comment_omitted_blocks: No `sharepoint` and no `teams` block, deliberately. Phase 1 provisions no
SharePoint site (the four tables hold no documents — DocuSign and file storage are
later phases) and no Microsoft Team: the only Teams usage is a 1:1 chat
notification sent to the process owner through the Teams connector (TAD ADR-015),
which needs a connection reference in pac-import-prd.json, not a provisioned team.
There is also no `code` app entry — Phase 1 ships the model-driven app only.
The pipeline therefore calls no sharepoint/* or teams/* script.
